demo_tour_keys: Use the left and right arrow keys to move between steps, Escape to close.
demo_tour_s1_body: The overview reads like a forecast: one sentence for the whole estate, and below it only the things worth your attention. A quiet sky means you can close the tab.
demo_tour_s1_title: The weather, then what needs you
demo_tour_s2_body: This Proxmox cluster shows nodes, guests, storage, replication and backups on one page, from the same API the real collector reads. Every chart has the last seven days.
demo_tour_s3_body: Rules come ready-made. A switch that goes down silences everything behind it; seasonal baselines learn what a normal Tuesday looks like; forecasts warn a disk will fill before it does.
demo_tour_s4_body: Email, ntfy, Matrix, Discord, Slack, Telegram, Gotify, webhooks and more — with quiet hours and per-device overrides. The demo never sends anything.
demo_tour_s5_body: Pick a type from the catalogue — hypervisors, NAS, firewalls, servers, printers, websites — and the form asks only for what that type needs. SNMP devices are recognised on their own.
demo_tour_s6_body: One small binary for Linux and Windows pushes CPU, disks, services and containers. It can also relay probes from a remote site that the server cannot reach.
demo_tour_s7_body: Publish a public page for your users, with incidents, uptime badges and email subscriptions — without exposing the rest of the instance.
demo_tour_s8_body: For a screen in the room: the bulletin full screen, readable from across it, with an optional music player. That is the tour — look around, nothing you click can break.

deviceform_discovery_intro: Enter your local network range and scan. DumbMonit looks for devices answering SNMP with the community above, then lets you add them all at once.
deviceform_discovery_none_desc: Check the range and the community, and make sure SNMP is enabled on the devices — the panel on the right explains how.
deviceform_discovery_range_help: In CIDR notation. Up to 4096 addresses per scan.
deviceform_discovery_scanning_note: Scanning {cidr}. A /24 takes a few seconds.
deviceform_discovery_unavailable_desc: Update the server to scan, or pick a type on the left and add devices one by one.
deviceform_discovery_unavailable_title: This server cannot scan networks yet
deviceform_edit_type_fixed: Type cannot be changed: remove the device and add it again as another type.
deviceform_enroll_compose_note: Or run the agent as a container at the site, with {file} from the repository — relay mode included:
deviceform_enroll_copy_now: Copy the command now: this token will not be displayed again.
deviceform_enroll_done_note: The agent registers itself as a device within a minute. You can close this page. This token enrols this one machine and nothing else; for a fleet, create a reusable token in Settings → Agents.
deviceform_enroll_intro: A server with the agent has no address to enter: the agent installed on the machine introduces itself to this server. Create a token, run the command it gives you, done.
deviceform_enroll_origin_note: The commands below point the agent at {origin}, the address of this page. If the site reaches this server at another address — usually a public HTTPS name — replace it before running them.
deviceform_enroll_relay_intro: A relay is an ordinary agent with one more setting. Placed on a machine at another site — a second office, a client, a VPS — it runs this server's probes from there and sends back the results. It only connects out: no port to open, no VPN.
deviceform_enroll_site_help: Shown next to the relay when you pick it for a device.
deviceform_enroll_step1: Install the agent on a machine at the remote site
deviceform_enroll_step3: Add the devices of that site
deviceform_enroll_step3_note: The relay appears among the devices within a minute. Add each switch, NAS or hypervisor there as usual, with its address as seen from the site, and under More options set "Reached through" to the relay. Nothing needs opening at the site: the relay only connects out.
deviceform_enroll_token_help: One token can enrol several machines: name it after a group or a machine.
deviceform_enroll_token_help_relay: Only used to recognise the token in Settings → Agents.
deviceform_enroll_yaml_note: Add these two lines to its {file} ({linux} on Linux, {unix} on macOS and FreeBSD, {windows} on Windows), then restart the agent.
deviceform_feature_backups_next: Install the agent on a machine that can open the repositories, then list them under “restic_repos:” or “borg_repos:” in its agent.yaml, with a password file. The password never leaves the machine.
deviceform_feature_backups_summary: Age of the last snapshot of each repository, and whether it can still be read.
deviceform_feature_disks_next: The agent reads SMART with smartctl: install smartmontools on the machine. The installed service has the rights it needs; sleeping disks are never woken.
deviceform_feature_disks_summary: Wear, reallocated and pending sectors, temperature: a drive warns weeks before it fails.
deviceform_feature_docker_next: The agent reads the containers from the Docker socket. Install it on the machine that runs Docker: they appear on that machine’s page.
deviceform_feature_docker_summary: State, health, restarts and image updates of every container, with restart and update from here.
deviceform_feature_hyperv_next: Install the agent on the Hyper-V host (Windows Server or Windows with the Hyper-V role): it finds the vmms service and reads Hyper-V’s performance counters on its own. The Hyper-V panel appears on that machine’s page.
deviceform_feature_hyperv_summary: Virtual machines in critical health, the host’s real CPU load with its guests, memory of each VM and virtual disk errors.
deviceform_feature_plakar_next: The agent finds Plakar and its klosets on its own. Install it on the machine that runs the backups: the Backups panel appears on its page.
deviceform_feature_plakar_summary: Age, count and state of the snapshots in each kloset, found without any setup.
deviceform_feature_relay_next: Install the agent on any machine at the remote site, then switch it to relay mode. Add the devices of that site as usual, with their local address, and pick the agent under More options → Reached through.
deviceform_feature_relay_summary: An agent at a second site, a client’s office or behind a NAT probes the devices there for this server. Outbound only.
deviceform_feature_sensors_next: The agent reads the probes the system exposes, on Linux, macOS and FreeBSD; fan speeds on Linux only. Windows exposes none.
deviceform_feature_sensors_summary: The machine’s own temperature probes against their critical point, and fan speeds.
deviceform_feature_services_next: Install the agent, then name the services to watch under “services:” in its agent.yaml. Failed systemd units are reported without any list.
deviceform_feature_services_summary: systemd units, Windows services, launchd and rc.d services, running or stopped.
deviceform_feature_updates_next: The agent reads them with dnf or apt, on Fedora, RHEL, Debian and Ubuntu families.
deviceform_feature_updates_summary: Pending and security updates, a reboot waiting, failed units, SELinux mode.
deviceform_feature_wireguard_next: The agent reads the tunnels with wg show, on Linux: install it on the machine that runs WireGuard. Peers with a persistent keepalive alert when they go silent.
deviceform_feature_wireguard_summary: Every peer of every interface: time since its last handshake, traffic, and tunnels gone silent.
deviceform_feature_zfs_next: The agent reads the pools with zpool, on Linux, FreeBSD or TrueNAS. Install it on the machine that holds them.
deviceform_feature_zfs_summary: Pool state, fill, device errors and the age of the last scrub.

deviceform_new_door_scan_desc: Give a range like 192.168.1.0/24: every device answering SNMP is listed, ready to add.

status_action_confirm_done: You are subscribed. Every message has a link to unsubscribe.
status_action_confirm_lead: Press the button to receive incident and maintenance updates from this status page by email.
status_action_link_incomplete: This link is incomplete. Open it again from the email you received.
status_action_link_invalid: This link is no longer valid. Subscribe again from the status page.
status_action_unsub_done: You are unsubscribed. No more emails will be sent to this address.
status_action_unsub_lead: Press the button to stop receiving updates from this status page.
status_domain_help: Optional. Your own address for this page, served through your reverse proxy.
status_domain_https: HTTPS is handled by your proxy: links in emails and feeds use {scheme}. If the domain shows the DumbMonit sign-in screen instead of the page, the proxy is not passing the Host header on; a bare "Not found" means it rewrites the path.
status_domain_live_when: once your proxy sends it here.
status_domain_step_dns: Create the DNS record for the name (or the public hostname of a Cloudflare Tunnel), pointing at your reverse proxy.
status_domain_step_host: Pass the original {header} header on. Nginx Proxy Manager, Traefik, Caddy and Cloudflare Tunnel do it by default; with plain Nginx add {directive}.
status_domain_step_proxy: In the proxy, send the name to the address of DumbMonit, for example {url}, without rewriting the path.
status_domain_what_body: Visitors who open this address see this status page straight away, at the root. Nothing else of DumbMonit answers there: no sign-in, no settings, no other page.
status_edit_description: Change what the page shows; visitors see it within a minute.
status_edit_new_description: Pick the services to show and the labels visitors will read. The page stays a draft until you publish it.
status_embed_not_found: This status page does not exist.
status_form_accent_help: Links, the top rule and the subscribe button. Each accent stays readable by day and by night.
status_form_description_help: One sentence under the title. Optional.
status_form_description_placeholder: What is up at home, at a glance.
status_form_domain_rule: The host name only, like status.example.com: no path, port or space.
status_form_footer_help: Plain text under the page, up to 280 characters: who runs it, how to reach them.
status_form_history_help: Longest window. The page shows as many days as its data covers, from 7 up to this.
status_form_homepage_help: Optional link shown next to the title.
status_form_logo_help: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 256 KiB. Square works best.
status_form_logo_read: The file could not be read.
status_form_logo_size: The logo is limited to {kib} KiB.
status_form_logo_type: Use a PNG, JPEG or WebP image.
status_form_published_on: Anyone with the link can see it.
status_form_rotation_help: With several scenes ticked, which one a visitor sees and when it changes. They follow the order in which you ticked them.
status_form_scene_help: An optional illustrated city behind the title of the public page. New pages start on Paris; untick it for a plain page. Ignored in simple mode. Tick several to alternate between them.
status_form_services_empty: No device yet. Add one on the Devices page first.
status_form_services_help: Tick the devices to show. The label is what visitors read; a group heads a block of services.
status_form_simple_help: A plain page: no scene, no mascot, no animation. Light or dark follows the visitor's system, with a toggle.
status_form_slug_rule: 2 to 40 characters: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
status_form_subscribers_help: Visitors confirm their address by email, and every update carries a one-click unsubscribe link.
status_form_subscribers_no_channel: Add an email (SMTP) channel under Notifications to let visitors subscribe. Until then the page offers its RSS feed.
status_incidents_body_placeholder_mainte: Firmware upgrade on the router; expect a short outage.
status_incidents_empty_description: Open an incident when something breaks, or schedule a maintenance window ahead of time.
status_incidents_first_message_help: Optional. What visitors read under the title.
status_incidents_impact_major: Major — the page shows an outage
status_incidents_lead: Announcements shown at the top of a page — or of every page.
status_incidents_window_order: The end must come after the start.
status_incidents_window_required: A maintenance window needs a start and an end.
status_list_description: Public pages that show whether your services are up, with a 90-day history and your announcements. No sign-in needed to read them.
status_list_empty_description: Create one, pick the services to show, then share the link.
status_list_load_error: Could not load the status pages
status_list_pages_description: Each page shows only the services you put on it, under the labels you choose.
status_list_saved_draft: still a draft, visitors get a 404 until you publish it.
status_public_load_error: Could not load the status page
status_public_no_incident: No incident in the last 30 days.
status_public_no_service_description: This page has nothing to show for now.
status_public_not_found_description: Check the link you were given, or ask whoever runs this DumbMonit for the right one.
status_public_not_found_title: This status page does not exist.
status_share_description: Badges for a README and a compact view to embed in an intranet page.
status_share_embed_hint: Add {light} or {dark} to match the host page, {history} to hide the bars.
status_subscribers_empty_description: Visitors subscribe from the bottom of the public page.
status_updates_email_lead: An email when an incident or a maintenance is announced or changes. Unsubscribe from any message.
status_updates_rate_limited: Too many requests from here. Try again in a few minutes.
status_uptime_bar_label: {label}: uptime per day over {days} days. Use the arrow keys to move between days.

wall_music_play_error: Spotify did not start playing here.
wall_music_speaker_label: Use this display as a Spotify speaker

wall_refresh_failed: Last refresh failed, showing the previous state.
wall_theme_forced: A link set this one for right now; it is not saved here.

devices_ad_bind_hint: Nothing else is read until the account can log in again. Read {when}.
devices_ad_bind_text: {host} answers but refuses the service account: {error}.
devices_ad_dcs_desc: Every domain controller of the domain, from the configuration partition, and whether its LDAP port answers.
devices_ad_findings_desc: Raw facts read from the directory, most severe first. Account findings come from the full inventory, read in the background.
devices_ad_groups_desc: Effective members, nested groups included, found by their well-known identifier whatever the domain's language.
devices_ad_inventory_loading: The full inventory of accounts is being read in the background.
devices_ad_inventory_pending: The full inventory has not completed yet; policy and infrastructure checks found nothing.
devices_ad_no_dc: No domain controller could be read from the configuration partition.
devices_ad_no_finding: No finding: nothing in the directory matches a known weakness.
devices_ad_repl_single: A single domain controller: nothing to replicate.
devices_ad_repl_unreadable: Not readable: the service account lacks the Monitor active directory replication right.
devices_ad_unread: The domain has not been read yet.
devices_adguard_check_off: The version check is off on this installation (as in the Docker image): updates are not tracked.
devices_adguard_err_title: Could not load AdGuard Home's state
devices_adguard_filter_lists_off: Filter lists: filtering is turned off in the general settings
devices_adguard_never_one: One enabled list was never downloaded: it blocks nothing.
devices_adguard_never_other: {count} enabled lists were never downloaded: they block nothing.
devices_adguard_protection_off: Protection: turned off, nothing is filtered
devices_adguard_upstreams_none: No upstream answered in the statistics window, and the upstream test is off.
devices_agent_bound_detail: This agent holds a secret of its own. No other machine can push measurements in its name, or pick up its container commands.
devices_agent_description: The machine as its agent describes it, and how the server knows it is really this one.
devices_agent_err_rebind: Could not open the re-enrolment window
devices_agent_rebind_hint_bound: Use this after reinstalling the machine, or when the agent lost the secret it had. It opens a short window during which the agent binds itself again.
devices_agent_rebind_hint_unbound: Opens a one-hour window during which this host's agent binds itself at its next batch.
devices_agent_too_old: The installed agent ({version}) is too old to be bound: re-run the install command on this host as well.
devices_agent_unbound_detail: This host was enrolled before agent binding and never bound to its agent, so the server now refuses its measurements, container commands and relayed probes. Allow re-enrolment, then restart the agent: its next batch binds the host.
devices_agent_window_open: Re-enrolment is open until {until}. The next batch from an agent with a valid token will bind this machine again.
devices_clients_description: Last connection and last backup, per device.
devices_clients_empty_desc: Devices appear here once the integration has read at least one connection or backup.
devices_docker_cancel_title: Pull the command back before the agent picks it up
devices_docker_err_action: The action could not be sent
devices_docker_last_none: none yet — policies act on their own, or restart and update from the container list.
devices_docker_needs_agent: Restart and update need an agent that runs commands.
devices_docker_no_metric: No metric for this container in this range.
devices_docker_none: No Docker on this machine, or the agent cannot reach its socket (add the agent to the docker group or run it as root).
devices_docker_recent_none: Nothing yet. Open a container and restart or update it.
devices_docker_strip_unavailable: This agent cannot run commands (too old, or commands: false): policies are kept but nothing runs until it is reinstalled with the current installer.
devices_docker_unavailable_body: This agent cannot run commands — {why}. Reinstall it with the current installer (token from Settings → Agents, commands: true); restart, update and the policies below stay off until it reports back.
devices_docker_update_all: Auto-update in maintenance windows, all containers
devices_docker_update_how: Updates pull the same tag, recreate the container, wait for its healthcheck and roll back if it fails; the old image is removed afterwards.
devices_docker_why_disabled: agent {version} reports actions disabled (commands: false) or predates the command channel
devices_docker_why_unknown: no agent has reported its capabilities yet
devices_docker_window_link: schedule one on the Alerts page
devices_docker_window_note: Auto-update only runs inside a maintenance window for this device —
devices_ha_all_ok: Nothing needs attention: no low battery, no update waiting, no open repair.
devices_ha_first_50: Only the first 50 are named; the counts below include them all.
devices_k8s_desc_version: Kubernetes {version}, read from its API server.
devices_k8s_healthy_text: Every node is ready and every workload has its replicas.
devices_mail_counters_none: No counters read: the API describes none, or the account that owns the key may not read them. Give that account the Global Administrator role if they stay empty.
devices_mail_counters_off: Counter reading is turned off in this device's options.
devices_mail_desc: Checked from outside, as a mail client would.
devices_mail_error: Could not load the mail services
devices_mail_no_ports: No port is checked on this device: its Services option is set to none.
devices_mail_op_note: The account may not run GetVersionInfo; the version still comes from the answer.
devices_mail_queues_hint: Queue sizes are not visible from outside: install the DumbMonit agent on this server and they appear here. If they do not, make that agent the parent of this device.
devices_mail_version_unknown: Version unknown: the greeting does not announce it.
